## Claims
- [source-backed] The full-coordinate Hopf input gives coproduct/antipode identities in \(\Lambda\), with \(S(s_\lambda)=(-1)^{|\lambda|}s_{\lambda'}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735]
- [source-backed] The full-coordinate row map is \(T(A_{\lambda,\theta})=\bar s_\lambda\otimes\bar s_\theta\), and decomposable rows map to \(\mathrm{CP}(\bar s_{\nu_B}\otimes\bar s_{\nu_R})\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 373-397; 442-493]
- [proved] The intended statement is: for \(q=n-r\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\), and \(\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a)\subseteq b^a\),
  \[
  [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]=(-1)^{|\rho|}
  [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}]\quad\text{in }Q. \tag{E}
  \]
  Here \(\rho'_k=\#\{\ell:\rho_\ell\ge k\}\); zero parts are omitted; and \(i^0\) is omitted when \(b=j\).
- [proved] Both partitions in (E) lie in \(q^r\): \((i^j,\rho)\) has width at most \(i\le q\) and length at most \(j+a\le r\); the right partition has width at most \(i+a\le q\) and length \(j\le r\).
- [proved] Define the two-sided rectangle attachment
  \[
  \operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\sigma,\tau)
  :=(i+\tau'_1,\ldots,i+\tau'_b,i^{j-b},\sigma),
  \qquad \sigma,\tau\subseteq b^a.
  \]
  Then \(\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\rho,\varnothing)=(i^j,\rho)\) and \(\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\varnothing,\rho)=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})\).
- [proved] The supplied Hopf identity does not itself supply a termwise identity
  \[
  s_{(i^j,\rho)}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\varnothing,\rho)}
  \in\sum_{\sigma\subsetneq\rho}\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\sigma|}s_{(i^j,\sigma)}. \tag{R}
  \]
  Its terms are tensors/row vectors \(\mathrm{CP}(s_\lambda\otimes s_{\mu'})\), whereas (R) requires a separately defined and proved map from those terms to Schur-function multiples with lower attachment \(\sigma\).
- [unsupported] No supplied source passage, accepted full-coordinate row identity, or graded-kernel presentation provides the required coefficients \(F_{\rho,\sigma}\), proves their integrality, or proves that all non-endpoint terms in (R) have \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\).

## Strategy
For \(\rho=\varnothing\) (including \(a=0\)), both sides of (E) equal \([\bar s_{i^j}]\). For \(b=j\), the suffix \(i^{j-b}=i^0\) is empty.

The required repair would need a new rectangular-straightening lemma (R), with an explicit integral expansion
\[
s_{(i^j,\rho)}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\varnothing,\rho)}
=\sum_{\sigma\subsetneq\rho}F_{\rho,\sigma}s_{(i^j,\sigma)},
\quad F_{\rho,\sigma}\in\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\sigma|}.
\]
Only after that lemma is established may projection to \(A\) place its right side in \(A_+J_v\), and then projection to \(Q\) yield (E).

## Gaps
The required termwise rectangular-straightening derivation is absent. In particular, neither endpoint coefficients \(1\) and \(-(-1)^{|\rho|}\) nor the asserted lower-attachment support have been proved from the supplied Hopf row identity. Therefore (E) is not established or disproved by this certificate.

## Next
A valid replacement must provide an explicit integral rectangular Laplace/Plücker or determinantal expansion proving (R) term by term.
